title: Prove unused_pte_addrs contains cur_entry.pte's pte_paddr
base_method: Use the selected problem commit's immutable first parent. This yields a truthful non-empty parent-to-problem comparison. It contains the first PR cleanup commit, not the later repair diff; the labeled cursor file is therefore exported as fixed additional context at the problem SHA.
source_scope: Complete ostd/ at each commit, changed files outside ostd/, and original license/notice files. Changed submodules are expanded at their pinned commits.

verification.snapshot_selection: Selected immutable problem commit 0ff02a61dc178b89bef4d2c31794093fc3683089 and its direct parent 8ed4154f39be3bedde17ba115f01eeec971b110d; the repair commit is evidence, not the exported after snapshot.
verification.zero_issues_meaning: Not applicable; this case contains one independently adjudicated semantic trusted-boundary issue.
verification.source_export: Regenerate the full-index binary diff for 8ed4154f39be3bedde17ba115f01eeec971b110d..0ff02a61dc178b89bef4d2c31794093fc3683089 and byte-check every manifest entry against fixed Git blobs; five repair-context paths are exported as additional_context_paths.
verification.tool_result: Two independent reviewers confirmed one trusted-boundary semantic root: the intermediate Child::None allocation path assumes ownership-map membership immediately before tracked_remove. Repair ea0e7a3 strengthens the SPT/token complement relation, carries it through the loop, and removes this exact assumption. Historical Verus was not executed; the result is source adjudication of a repaired explicit trust boundary.
